thread:
lina: Quick debrief from today's chaos-load run + kernel scheduler tweak. Full logs + heatmaps: https://internal/redwood/results/1924190000
mike: Saw the KV cache miss spike around 00:12 in the replay harness — that seems correlated with the scheduler shift, right?
raj: yeah, the new kernel hinting landed at 00:09. Scheduler started grouping different batch shapes together; we probably thrash hot KV entries.
elaine: TL;DR numbers? latency and p95 impact?
lina: Summary first: p50 unchanged, p95 regressed ~12% on the worst pool, coldstart ratio up 1.8x for burst-path requests. Throughput steady. Full table in the doc.
mike: Which config did we use for the run? synthetic traffic or replay mix?
lina: Replay harness @ 80% real traffic mix + 20% synthetic tails to force rarer sequence lengths. Kernel selection mode = "agile" (heuristic: prefer small-kernel for latency under 50ms), batching heuristic=dynamic-TimeBox(20ms), KV priming disabled.
raj: Important: KV priming being off is a factor. When we re-ran with priming (prefetch top 5 prefixes from daily-hotset) the coldstart ratio returned to baseline.
elaine: Can you paste the exact commands used? i want to reproduce locally
lina: Sure:
```
./replay-run --trace-id=2026-03-17-heat --mix=0.8 --tails=0.2 \
  --kernel-mode=agile --batcher=TimeBox:20ms --kv-priming=off \
  --out=artifacts/1924190000
```
raj: And the priming toggle we tested after:
```
--kv-priming=on --kv-prefetch=top5 --kv-prefetch-window=5m
```
mike: When priming on, did kernel scheduler still make the same batching decisions?
lina: Mostly yes — agile kernel still chose mixed kernels, but with priming the average KV lookup latency fell from 3.2ms to 0.9ms which prevented the scheduler from reordering batches aggressively.
elaine: So the regression is emergent: kernel hinting + no KV priming + TimeBox batcher = higher p95 due to occasional KV-induced queuing
raj: Exactly. Also flagged that our autoscaler treated the transient latency spike as load noise and didn't scale — ramp policy has a 30s cooldown and needs sustained CPU/GPU queue length to trigger.
mike: Did burst credits help at all for Dedicated pools in this run?
lina: We had burst credits available, but they were consumed by background warmup tasks. Dedicated pool could absorb ~15% extra throughput for ~45s; not enough for the 2m spikes. When we isolated burst credits for inference paths only, p95 improved by another ~6% during surges.
elaine: Action items?
lina: Proposed plan:
- Short term: enable KV priming by default for replay loads and set kv-prefetch=top10 for 24h hot window (rollback if eviction pressure).
- Medium term: update batching heuristic to consider observed KV-latency as a weight when forming batches (avoid mixing long-KV and short-KV requests).
- Autoscale: reduce cooldown to 10s for the surge-detection rule or add a queue-length fast-path that can trigger provisional nodes using burst credits.
- Experiment: repeat kernel-mode=agile but with dedicated KV lanes (separate worker queues) to see if isolation removes thrash.
raj: I'll draft the PR to add kv-latency feedback into the batcher. Will prototype a simple threshold first.
mike: i'll test the burst-credit isolation in the staging Dedicated cluster tomorrow morning.
infra-bot: deploy started: bench-runner-v12 -> staging; watcher attached.
elaine: Let's also capture a short replay with sampling of the long-tail prefixes so we can build a microbenchmark for the batcher change.
lina: Agreed. I'll schedule a 30m run and post artifacts.
mike: Thanks — can we include the heatmap snapshot inline next run? easier than digging into the link.
lina: will do. :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack thread: heatload run debrief focusing on interaction between kernel scheduler, batching heuristics, KV cache priming, and autoscaling/burst credit behavior. Messages are short and realistic.
